messages:
roxanne: noticed a trickle of requests using the old Session-Proto: v1 header. v2 expects structured context JSON in body. those v1 requests hit runtime parsing assumptions and show up as parse_error.metric.

vikram: how many? any big tenants?

roxanne: ~1.1% last 7d, mostly a handful of small integrators and old SDKs. logged as session_proto.legacy.count.

kai: options: 1) runtime compatibility bridge that rewrites v1->v2 wrapper, 2) client-side migration docs + longer deprecation, 3) proxy shim per-tenant.

roxanne: proposing a lightweight bridge: detect header Session-Proto: v1, parse legacy KV pair body, synthesize JSON context, and set Session-Proto: v2 before regular handlers. gated behind feature flag and per-tenant opt-in.

sam: security ask: run bridge before auth parsing? we should convert first, then auth. also cap legacy payload to 8KB and reject larger.

vikram: telemetry: emit session_proto.detect, session_proto.converted, session_proto.rejected; tag tenant. add deprecation header: X-RW-Deprecation: session-proto; until=2027-10-01 when we accept a legacy request.

kai: runtime notes: implement as tiny C++ middleware, reuse parsing helpers from on-prem shim, allocate from a small preallocated buffer to avoid GC churn. add circuit-breaker: if converted p50 latency +5ms or error delta >0.4% for tenant, auto-disable.

roxanne: rollout: default off; canary to affected tenants first; console toggle compat.session_proto_bridge; billing tag compat.session_proto_cpu. lifecycle: support 5 months then 60-day removal notice.

ops-bot: scheduled staging deploy for branch: feature/session-proto-bridge (sha: d4e5f6)

vikram: tests: unit parsers, e2e migration path, load test with 10k legacy reqs/s. outreach: email the top three integrators with example transformation snippets.

roxanne: will draft RFC + playbook and link perf numbers. if no objections we'll canary next week.

kai: +1 from runtime provided limits and auth-after-convert.

vikram: assigning follow-ups: vikram -> RFC+outreach, kai -> perf microbench, sam -> security review.

roxanne: thanks everyone.
